inputs_used: Scan Report-6 validated and deduplicated findings
metadata.capacity_assumption: No capacity limit was provided. Queue assumes a default small-team sequence: remediate immediate process-compromise issues first, then auth/data exposure and defense-in-depth, while separately validating runtime-dependent candidates.

summary.priority_basis: Prioritization considered severity, confidence, exploitability, affected asset, exposed interface, threat-model convergence, security boundary impact, existing controls, relationships to other findings, and remediation complexity.

remediation_queue.title: Unauthenticated Python eval code execution
remediation_queue.affected_asset: Flask process authority, in-memory secrets, database cursor, host resources
remediation_queue.interface_exposure: Unauthenticated POST /evaluate; default bind is localhost but CLI can expose beyond localhost.
remediation_queue.threat_model_relevance: T1 and process-authority convergence. Compromise can subsume auth, DB, config, and key material.
remediation_queue.existing_controls: No authentication or sandbox before eval.
remediation_queue.relationship_to_other_findings: Can enable or bypass impacts covered by TF-005, TF-006, TF-008, TF-010, and TF-011 by directly accessing process state.
remediation_queue.priority_reasoning: This is the most direct unauthenticated path to full Python execution in the shared process. It has high confidence, minimal preconditions, broad blast radius, and weak or absent controls.
remediation_queue.recommended_action: Remove eval or replace with a constrained parser/evaluator; block route in deployable builds until fixed.

remediation_queue.title: OS command injection in DNS lookup
remediation_queue.affected_asset: Host command/process boundary and Flask process host environment
remediation_queue.existing_controls: No argument boundary, shell avoidance, or hostname validation.
remediation_queue.relationship_to_other_findings: Overlaps in impact with TF-001 and TF-003 but uses a distinct OS command boundary.
remediation_queue.priority_reasoning: This is a direct unauthenticated host command path. It ranks just below eval because it depends on shell/OS command behavior, but the exploitability and impact remain immediate.
remediation_queue.recommended_action: Replace shell command with a DNS library or subprocess argument list with shell disabled; validate hostnames/IPs.

remediation_queue.title: Pickle deserialization of client cookie
remediation_queue.existing_controls: Base64 encoding only; no integrity or safe serialization.
remediation_queue.relationship_to_other_findings: Same process-compromise class as TF-001 and TF-002, but requires a crafted cookie request rather than form input.
remediation_queue.priority_reasoning: Client-controlled pickle deserialization is a high-confidence code execution primitive with a straightforward fix. It should be handled in the first remediation batch.
remediation_queue.recommended_action: Replace pickle cookie state with signed JSON/Flask session or server-side state.

remediation_queue.title: Server-side template injection in greeting route
remediation_queue.affected_asset: Template execution context and Flask process state
remediation_queue.existing_controls: No fixed template or variable binding; Jinja receives attacker-influenced template source.
remediation_queue.relationship_to_other_findings: Can converge with TF-001 through process-level access, but root cause is template-source compilation.
remediation_queue.priority_reasoning: Although reported as high rather than critical, exploitability is strong and remediation is small. It belongs in the immediate batch with other process-authority issues.
remediation_queue.recommended_action: Use a fixed template and pass name as escaped data.

remediation_queue.title: JWT algorithm confusion and None acceptance
remediation_queue.affected_asset: Authentication cookie, admin authorization state, JWT trust boundary
remediation_queue.interface_exposure: GET /user with attacker-supplied authentication cookie; /user/jwks exposes key material used in the trust context.
remediation_queue.existing_controls: Audience, issuer, time, and sub checks exist but do not defeat untrusted algorithm dispatch.
remediation_queue.relationship_to_other_findings: Combines with TF-010 if private key material is exposed, and TF-011/TF-009 if token theft occurs.
remediation_queue.priority_reasoning: This breaks the authentication boundary but currently only grants an admin response state, while process-compromise findings have broader blast radius. It should follow immediately after process RCE items.
remediation_queue.recommended_action: Pin to RS256 server-side, remove None/HS256 paths, and harden authorization decisions.

remediation_queue.title: SQL injection in listservices category filter
remediation_queue.existing_controls: No parameterization; try/except only reflects errors.
remediation_queue.relationship_to_other_findings: Related to TF-009 through the same route but separate control. Process-compromise findings could also reach database state indirectly.
remediation_queue.priority_reasoning: This is a direct unauthenticated database attack path. It ranks below RCE and auth-boundary bypass because backend behavior and privileges affect impact, but it remains near-term.
remediation_queue.recommended_action: Use parameterized queries and generic error handling across supported database drivers.

remediation_queue.title: Unsafe XML parser configuration
remediation_queue.affected_asset: Local files, network destinations, parser resource consumption
remediation_queue.existing_controls: Output escaping occurs after parse and does not protect parser resource handling.
remediation_queue.relationship_to_other_findings: Related to TF-002 by host/network resource reachability but uses XML parser behavior.
remediation_queue.priority_reasoning: Unsafe parser settings are easy to harden and sit on an unauthenticated route. Exact XXE/SSRF behavior is runtime-dependent, so it trails more deterministic RCE/auth/data findings.
remediation_queue.recommended_action: Disable DTD loading, network access, entity resolution, and huge_tree for untrusted XML; add request size limits.

remediation_queue.title: Raw HTML rendering of attacker-influenced values
remediation_queue.affected_asset: Browser session, authentication cookie exposure, UI integrity
remediation_queue.threat_model_relevance: Authentication/token exposure relationship with TF-011 and TF-006.
remediation_queue.existing_controls: No consistent autoescaped template rendering. Some XML output uses html.escape, but affected paths do not.
remediation_queue.relationship_to_other_findings: Amplifies TF-011 because the auth cookie is not HttpOnly; separate from TF-005 even where /listservices overlaps.
remediation_queue.priority_reasoning: XSS is important, especially because cookies are script-accessible, but the first queue should remove direct server-side execution and auth bypasses. Plan this with the template/output cleanup wave.
remediation_queue.recommended_action: Move HTML generation to autoescaped templates and avoid raw exception reflection.

remediation_queue.title: Predictable temporary JWT private key storage
remediation_queue.interface_exposure: Startup fallback when key-file env vars are absent; same-host/log exposure required.
remediation_queue.existing_controls: Configured key files avoid fallback, but fallback remains insecure.
remediation_queue.relationship_to_other_findings: Can enable token forgery and magnify TF-006; deployment-dependent candidate TC-003 should validate exposure.
remediation_queue.priority_reasoning: Key exposure is serious, but exploitability depends on same-host or log access and runtime configuration. Schedule after remotely reachable unauthenticated issues unless deployment review shows exposed temp/log state.
remediation_queue.recommended_action: Require explicit key management or generate in a private restricted directory without printing paths.

remediation_queue.title: AES-CBC config selector padding/decryption oracle
remediation_queue.affected_asset: Config selector integrity and hidden config values
remediation_queue.existing_controls: Only app_ keys are linked, but decrypted selectors are checked against all CONFIG keys; exceptions are returned.
remediation_queue.relationship_to_other_findings: May expose or aid access to config material, but process-compromise findings bypass it entirely.
remediation_queue.priority_reasoning: This is remotely reachable but lower impact in the current implementation because direct hidden byte-value rendering is constrained. It should be fixed as part of crypto/config cleanup.
remediation_queue.recommended_action: Use authenticated tokens/encryption, generic errors, and a strict allowlist.

remediation_queue.title: Authentication cookie missing Secure, HttpOnly, and SameSite
remediation_queue.threat_model_relevance: Authentication/token exposure relationship with TF-009 and TF-006.
remediation_queue.existing_controls: Cookie expiry is set, but security attributes are absent.
remediation_queue.relationship_to_other_findings: Amplifies XSS/token theft risk from TF-009; does not itself bypass auth.
remediation_queue.priority_reasoning: This is a quick hardening win but lower standalone impact than execution, injection, auth-bypass, or data-access issues. Bundle with auth hardening.
remediation_queue.recommended_action: Set HttpOnly, Secure under HTTPS, and SameSite appropriately.

validation_queue.title: Exact lxml external resource behavior
validation_queue.reasoning: Unsafe XML parser settings are confirmed, but exact file/network/XXE behavior depends on lxml/libxml2 runtime and deployment constraints.
validation_queue.recommended_action: Validate parser behavior in the supported runtime or harden immediately if runtime validation is not needed for decision-making.

validation_queue.title: Predictable temp key exposure on host
validation_queue.reasoning: Source writes predictable temp keys, but practical exploitation depends on temp directory ACLs, user separation, and logs.
validation_queue.recommended_action: Review deployment filesystem ACLs and log handling; raise TF-010 priority if private key path/content is exposed.

validation_queue.title: Live dependency vulnerability status
validation_queue.reasoning: Dependency CVE status was not checked during offline scans.
validation_queue.recommended_action: Run authorized SCA/advisory lookup for requirements.txt.

notes: If capacity is constrained to only three fixes, start with TF-001, TF-002, and TF-003.
If the application is exposed beyond localhost, keep all immediate and near-term items in the current sprint.
If this remains a local training-only app, still fix immediate items first because they dominate every other risk through shared process authority.
